input: Write a due diligence memo on Revolut

output.company: Revolut (Revolut Group Holdings Ltd; consolidated group)

business.claim: Scope: Revolut Group Holdings Ltd and its consolidated business. As of 2026-11-10, the holding company is an active UK private limited company, number 12743269, with its registered office in London.
Offers consumers app-based spending, saving, investing and international transfers.
Revolut Business sells multi-currency accounts, international payments, merchant payment acceptance, corporate cards, expense management and accounting integrations to businesses.
Business model combines card-payment income, subscriptions, foreign-exchange and wealth fees with interest income. Fee-based revenues represented 76% of turnover for the year ended 2025-12-31.
Company claim: as of 2026-11-04, banking operations spanned 30 EEA markets; banking launches during 2026 included the UK, Mexico, Australia and New Zealand.

traction.claim: Company claim: exceeded 80 million retail customers worldwide as of 2026-11-04; this is a customer count, not a disclosed active-user count.
Company claim: retail customers reached 68.3 million, up 30% year over year, and business customers reached 767,000, up 33%, as of 2025-12-31.
Company claim, published by partner Just Eat: Revolut had over 850,000 business customers as of 2026-10-28.
Company claim: the Business website displays Lyca, Deel, Aer Lingus, Wild, Dermalogica and Barry's as customer references; contract values and customer tenure are not disclosed.
Partner announcement, a company claim: Just Eat launched Revolut Pay account-to-account checkout in its UK and Ireland app on 2026-10-28.
Partner announcement, a company claim: Yuno integrated Revolut Pay, acquiring and gateway services through a single connection covering the UK, EEA, Singapore and Australia.

team.claim: As of 2026-11-10, co-founder Nik Storonsky is CEO. He launched Revolut in 2015 and previously traded equity derivatives at Credit Suisse and Lehman Brothers.
As of 2026-11-10, co-founder Vlad Yatsenko is a non-executive board member. His prior engineering experience includes UBS and Deutsche Bank.
Victor Stinga was identified as Revolut's CFO in the company's latest fundraising announcement.
As of 2026-11-10, Donato Lucia is VP of Technology. His previous employers include lastminute.com, IBM and HP.
As of 2026-11-10, Martin Gilbert chairs the board; he previously co-founded and led Aberdeen Asset Management.
Executive departure: Yatsenko stepped down as CTO effective 2026-07-01 while remaining a non-executive director; Lucia succeeded him with the title VP of Technology.
FinTech Futures reported the departure of head of expansion Dmytro Strelchuk after nearly eight years. He had joined from EY and was taking a career break.

funding.claim: Historical group financing, company claim: announced an $800 million Series E from SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and Tiger Global Management at a $33 billion valuation as of 2021-07-15.

Company claim: announced employee secondary-sale agreements at a $45 billion valuation as of 2024-08-16, led by Coatue, D1 Capital Partners and Tiger Global. This was shareholder liquidity, not an announced primary capital raise.
Company claim: completed a share sale at a $75 billion valuation as of 2025-11-24, led by Coatue, Greenoaks, Dragoneer and Fidelity Management & Research Company; employees could sell shares.

Latest completed transaction identified, company claim: fundraising closed at a $115 billion valuation as of 2026-11-04, led by Glade Brook Capital Partners, Coatue, Durable Capital Partners, accounts advised by T. Rowe Price Associates, and Baillie Gifford.
Reuters reported that Revolut declined to disclose how much money the latest transaction raised.

financial_signals.claim: Audited consolidated results for the year ended 2025-12-31: revenue £4.5 billion, up 46%; pretax profit £1.7 billion, up 57%; net profit £1.3 billion. These are reported results, not aggregator estimates.
Consolidated year-end headcount increased to 12,200 as of 2025-12-31 from 10,133 as of 2024-12-31.

Company regulatory disclosure: as of June 2026, CET1 capital was £5.7 billion and the CET1 ratio was 47.8%, versus 53.8% at December 2025. The disclosed liquidity coverage ratio was 176.3%, calculated using trailing monthly observations.
Financial News reported dozens of staff cuts in a performance-related cull as of 2026-11-04; Revolut said departures were in line with previous quarters.

Aggregator: Eurofound's European Restructuring Monitor records an announcement dated 2026-06-01 to recruit 200 employees in France, targeting completion by 2026-12-31. These are planned hires, not verified completed hires.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: AGCM named Revolut Group Holdings Ltd alongside relevant subsidiaries in penalties announced on 2026-04-02: €5 million for investment disclosures, €5 million for account-restriction practices and €1.5 million for Italian-IBAN disclosures. These are not parent-only penalty amounts.
Revolut disputed AGCM's findings and told FinTech Futures it would appeal in Italian courts. This establishes an announced intention, not a verified appeal filing or outcome.

As of 2025-12-31, the consolidated litigation, arbitration and regulatory provision was £22.754 million. The report withholds some case-specific estimates where disclosure could prejudice proceedings.

Company disclosure for FY2025: international expansion increases money-laundering and sanctions exposure; a French supervisory inspection prompted EEA-wide and global customer-due-diligence enhancements. This is not a sanctions-designation finding.

Brand-level security incident: CERT-EU reports that Revolut disclosed a customer-data breach on 2026-09-12 involving government-agency impersonation and exposure of identity documents, statements and transaction histories. The source does not establish holding-company liability.

reputation.claim: Employee-review aggregator Glassdoor displayed a 4.3/5 rating from 6,633 anonymous reviews as of 2026-11-10. This is a snapshot, not a verified longitudinal improvement or deterioration.

Glassdoor reviews dated 2026-11-07 praised learning opportunities but also described difficult work-life balance, high pressure and performance-management concerns. These are anonymous anecdotes, not independently established employment practices.

Customer-treatment concerns have regulatory support: AGCM found inadequate notice, opportunities to respond and assistance around account restrictions, sometimes leaving customers without access to funds for extended periods. Revolut disputes the findings.

Reuters' critical analysis highlighted lower revenue per customer than traditional banks and insufficient primary-account adoption. Revolut reported primary-account usage growth of 45% for FY2025 but declined to disclose the absolute customer count.

red_flags.claim: Assessment: AGCM's disputed findings create a concrete consumer-treatment and compliance diligence issue involving the holding company, particularly account access and product disclosures.

Assessment: the reported government-request impersonation breach warrants examination of disclosure-request authentication, sensitive-data access controls and remediation; holding-company liability remains unverified.

Assessment: headline customer scale does not establish depth of monetisation. Reuters' primary-account and revenue-per-customer findings warrant cohort, retention and customer-profitability diligence.

output.verdict: As of 2026-11-10, the cited evidence supports substantial customer scale, audited profitability and strong disclosed capitalisation. Advance to deeper diligence, but do not underwrite the headline valuation without examining financing terms, primary-account monetisation, consumer-treatment remediation and cybersecurity controls.

cost_basis: tokens x list price + $10 per 1K web search calls
